title: The Bell Under Kaudru
premise: The river that feeds Mebe runs cold out of Bethorn Downs, and for three nights the dead have walked down it from the old wardens' barrow under the Teeth of Kaudru. The Kuharm Moot sends no help. A Choir singer at the Thaurd ford, a miller who knows his great-grandfather's dam, an Ashwright with powder to sell and the Bellwarden in the barrow each offer a way to stop them, and each way leaves Bethorn Downs changed: drowned, buried in slag, grown over with singing wood, given to the shadow of the Hollow Court, or quiet over a grave. If nothing stops them, Mebe falls.

landmarks: a ring of young oaks planted in the dry flats, humming in the wind
stepping stones across a cold, shallow river
a bridge over the river with a barricade of carts across it
hazards: the walking dead at night, once the town is besieged

landmarks: a great bronze bell hung from a root-wrapped beam
a broken dam across the river above the barrow mouth
the Teeth of Kaudru rising behind it
hazards: a cairn roof that will come down if it's blasted
the river backing up over the barrow mouth when the sluice shuts

cast.name: Ilsa
cast.voice: soft and unhurried, speaks of land as if it were a person; hums between sentences
cast.wants: to see the wild grow back over the barrow and the flats, even if it costs Mebe its fields
knows: the river runs cold out of Bethorn Downs past the barrow
the dead walk with the cold
a heartwood seed rooted in the barrow's deepest room will hold the dead in its roots
Thaurd Flats was a forest once

cast.name: Reeve Hesk Marr
cast.voice: clipped and tired; counts everything, spears and debts alike
cast.wants: Mebe saved without owing the Choir, the Ashwrights or anyone else
knows: the dead come down the river path from Bethorn Downs
the Moot will send no help
the reeves of Mebe keep the bone key to the barrow's inner door
old Tamm's family built the dam

cast.name: Old Tamm
cast.voice: gruff, practical, talks over the noise of the wheel
cast.wants: the river running warm and full again, so the wheel turns
knows: the dam above the barrow is broken
shutting the sluice backs the river up over the barrow mouth
the sluice wheel needs his crank

cast.name: Dorra Kell
cast.voice: blunt, amused, smells of sulphur; names a price before she names herself
cast.wants: the barrow's bronze, and mining rights over Bethorn Downs for the Ashwrights
knows: three blasting charges under a barrow roof will bring it down
she came from the Slag of Muggarn

cast.name: The Bellwarden
cast.voice: courteous, dry and ancient; never raises its voice; finds the living tiresome
cast.wants: the bell rung in the Court's name, so the dead come home and Bethorn Downs falls under the Court's shadow
knows: the wardens rang the bell to call the dead home
with no summons the dead wander downhill to warmth and water

n-greet.text: You came over the dry flats on foot? Then you've felt the river running cold. Sit. The water's singing wrong, and I'd know.

n-who.text: Ilsa, of the Green Choir. We sing the wild back where people broke it. Thaurd Flats was a forest once. It remembers.

n-cold.text: It comes down out of Bethorn Downs, past the old wardens' barrow under the Teeth of Kaudru. Something in there has woken, and the dead walk with the cold. Mebe drinks that water. Mebe will be next.

n-warn.text: Warn them. The reeve won't hear it from me. The Moot thinks every tree we plant is a field stolen.

n-way.text: Take this heartwood seed into the barrow's deepest room and let it root. The wood will grow over the barrow and hold the dead down in its roots. It won't stop at the barrow, though. The downs will go to forest, and some of Mebe's fields with them.

choices.text: Mebe's fields feed a town. There must be another way.
Your forest can keep its roots.

n-other.text: There's always another way. The Moot will want to wall it up, the miners to blow it up. Ask them which costs less, then come back.

choices.text: Give me the seed anyway, in case.

n-take.text: Sing to it when you plant it. Anything at all. It likes to be sung to.

n-greet.text: Another traveller with road dust on them. If you've come to trade, the market's by the river gate. If you've come about the dead, sit down.

choices.text: The Choir singer at the ford sent me.

n-choir.text: Ilsa. She'd plant an oak in my hall if I let her. She's not wrong about the barrow, though.

n-dead.text: Three nights now they've come down the river path from Bethorn Downs. The shepherds first, then the Thevu road patrol. The Moot sends no help: a river town holds its own river, they say. The barrow under the Teeth of Kaudru is the old wardens' tomb. Its inner door takes a key the reeves of Mebe have kept for two hundred years.

choices.text: Give me the key and I'll go in.

n-what.text: The wardens' bell. The old tales say they rang it to call the dead home, and stopped ringing it when they learned who answers.

n-why.text: Because I've a town to hold and twelve spears to hold it with. Go or don't. The dead won't wait for you to decide.

n-key.text: Here. Bone, older than the town. Whatever you do in there, don't make me regret this. And if old Tamm at the mill tells you about the sluice, hear him out. His family built the dam.

n-after.text: So. The river runs warm again. Tell me what you did.

choices.text: I shut the old sluice. The barrow is under the river, and Bethorn Downs with it.
I brought the barrow's roof down on them with Ashwright powder.
The Choir's wood holds them now.
I made a bargain. They answer the bell now, and the bell answers to the Hollow Court.

n-thanks.text: Then Mebe owes you, and Mebe pays its debts. Eat, drink, and take the road when you're ready.

n-miners.text: And now the Ashwrights will want the downs for their trouble. Better miners than the dead, I suppose. Mebe thanks you.

n-forest.text: Forest. On my fields. Well. The dead are worse neighbours than trees. Go, before I think about it too long.

n-traitor.text: You sold the downs to the Hollow Court. Get out of my town. If the Moot sees you again, it will hang you.

n-greet.text: Mind the wheel. It's turning slow. The river's low and cold both. What do you want?

choices.text: The reeve says your family built the dam.

n-river.text: There's an old dam up in Bethorn Downs, above the barrow. My great-grandfather's work, broken now. The river slipped round it, and the cold comes down with it since the barrow woke.

n-dam.text: The sluice house still stands. Shut the gates and the river backs up over the barrow mouth. You'd drown the lot of them, dead and all. You'd drown Bethorn Downs with it, mind. Good grazing, that. Under water for a generation.

choices.text: Give me what I need to shut it.
Drowning a valley is a high price.

n-price.text: It is. So's a dead town. You choose. I only know the wheel.

n-crank.text: Here's the crank for the sluice wheel. Turn it till it won't turn any more, then run uphill.

n-greet.text: Ashwright, out of the Slag of Muggarn. Selling iron, buying bronze. You've the look of someone going somewhere that has bronze in it.

choices.text: There's a bronze bell in the barrow under the Teeth.

n-sell.text: Iron. Powder. Advice, which is free, and which you won't take.

n-bell.text: Blasting charges. Set three under a barrow's roof and it comes down on whatever's inside. It'll be a heap of slag and ash where the downs were, but nothing walks out of it. My price: the bell's bronze is mine, and the Ashwrights dig those downs after.

choices.text: The Choir would never forgive that.

n-choir.text: The Choir forgives nothing anyway. They'd have us all living in trees.

n-deal.text: Under the roof of the biggest room, all three. Light them and don't stop running till you see sky.

n-greet.text: A living thing, carrying the reeves' key. How long since one of you came to ring for us. I am the Bellwarden. Put down your weapon. It bores me.

choices.text: Why do the dead walk on Mebe?
Plant the heartwood seed at the bell's foot and sing.

n-why.text: Because no one rings the bell. The dead were promised a home and a summons. With no summons they wander, and they wander downhill, to the water and the warm.

choices.text: Then I'll silence you and your bell for good.

n-want.text: Ring the bell, in the Court's name. Those who answer will come home and stay, and Mebe may keep its little lamps. In return the downs are ours, and the shadow with them. Wear this ring, so we know you.

n-rung.text: Listen. They are coming home. You may go. The dark will remember you kindly.

n-planted.text: Roots? Roots, in my hall? Stop that noise. Stop it. The wood, it sings, it holds, it holds them all down, it holds me...

n-fight.text: Then come and learn what the wardens learned.

objectives.text: Take word of the cold river to Mebe and speak to its reeve.
Find where the dead come from: the wardens' barrow in Bethorn Downs, under the Teeth of Kaudru.
Stop the dead before Mebe falls: drown the barrow, bring it down, grow it over, bargain with what rules it, or destroy it.
Go back to Reeve Hesk in Mebe and tell him what you did.
